objective: Test whether two independent 5x4 contradiction families share a relabeling-covariant residual motif: an orientation between two equal-height open-cap holes, and whether the same motif occurs on cycle-supporting binary groups in flat controls.
rationale: The predecessor minimum contradiction and the support-release-surviving contradiction use different literal residual masks, so a literal-token law is excluded.
In both frozen representative families the varying residuals appear to be one-hole subsets of the current open-cap set.
A two-hole orientation can be described covariantly under column relabeling as an unordered equal-height hole pair plus sheet-specific choice, avoiding raw-mask identity as authority.
Flat nonvacuous controls can falsify sufficiency without importing solved outcomes.
targeted_observations: exact same-support sheet-pair residual symmetric differences
whether all varying residuals are one-hole subsets of the open-cap set
whether the two hole columns form an equal-height pair
count of such motifs across all binary groups in flat controls
count of such motifs on flat-control groups incident to undirected binary-cycle edges
open_observation_channel: Preserve flat cycle-supporting counterexamples as a falsifier; preserve absence as only a finite surviving candidate, not proof.
anti_circularity: The motif definition uses support heights and residual incidence only; it does not inspect syndrome/delta parity when classifying a state pair.
